label: GO step, choosing a2 after S2 was rewarded on the last trial
explanation: Fires almost only at GO (96% of activation mass; small weak tail at D1; never at D2), when the agent is about to choose a2 (model_act==2, strongly negative policy logit) and the previous trial ended in S2 and was rewarded (prev_reward==1, 99% of mass). Previous-trial state != 1 also lets in the first trial of each window, where the previous state is unknown. ep_trial>=10 drops early-episode trials, where it is nearly silent; activation rate rises over the episode. Every variable here is observed or is the agent own choice, so no future variable is used. Dev: P 0.88, R 0.84, F1 0.86, mass recall 0.91. Magnitude: the largest activations (about 1.0 of max) are on switches to a2 after a rewarded S2 visit (e.g. a1 went rarely to S2 and was rewarded, so the agent switches to a2). Those are about 3% of active steps but 6% of mass, so roughly twice the average. Repeated a2 choices after common-rewarded S2 trials fire more weakly (0.02-0.6). It does not fire for a1 choices, after unrewarded trials, after a rewarded S1 visit, or at D2.

issues: The core claims hold up (test split). It fires almost only at GO: D1 has 3.2% precision and 3.9% of the mass, D2 has zero activations. prev_reward==0 at GO gives P=0.000. a2 at GO after a rewarded S1 visit gives P=0.026. a1 choices hold 5.5% of the mass. Removing ep_trial drops F1 to 0.834. Using prev_state==2 alone, without the first window trial, drops recall to 0.65. The predicate's test scores match the reported ones: P 0.871, R 0.835, F1 0.853, mass recall 0.905.

The ep_trial >= 10 cutoff is in the wrong place. Firing switches on gradually around ep_trial 18-25, not at 10. Within the predicate, precision by ep_trial range is 0.07 (10-14), 0.32 (15-19), 0.69 (20-24), 0.87 (25-29) and 0.96 (30-39). So ep_trial 10-19 is a systematic block of false positives, about 12k predicted steps.

The magnitude story leaves out the main driver, episode position. Predicate steps with ep_trial >= 70 are 31% of active steps but carry 62% of the mass (P=0.989), while ep_trial 20-50 carries only about 10% of the mass. Switch versus stay is a smaller effect: at ep_trial >= 70, switches carry 4.6% of the mass on 1.7% of active steps, versus 44% of the mass on 22.7% for stays. So 'top activations are switches' is only half the picture. The feature grows steadily over the episode, and 'firing rate rises over the episode' understates this.

The remaining misses are weak and scattered. There is a D1 tail (about 7% of active steps, 2.5% of the mass) on trials whose upcoming choice is a2 after a reward. There is also a weak GO tail on a1 choices after rewards (5.5% of active steps, values around 0.1-0.16 of max), so 'does not fire on a1 choices' is slightly too strong. Neither gap is big enough to change the predicate.
The label is otherwise fine. It uses no future variables: model_act is the agent's own choice, and prev_* are observed.
